report.summary: Chunk 6 of 6 of drift.py: finalizes DriftReport with ignore/acceptance logic, defines refresh() and main() entry points.
risks: refresh() | medium | refresh() carries acceptances forward verbatim; claim 'never a way to quietly drop somebody's stated reason' is uncheckable because parsing of acceptances is not shown.
main() --init | medium | --init prints report and returns 0; but comment says 'matches `daedalus map --check`' which is uncheckable.

main() --init | high | --init returns 1 if snapshot exists; returns 0 otherwise. This matches behavior but the comment says 'write the FIRST baseline' but actually prints report and returns 0, not just writing baseline.
main() --refresh | low | --refresh calls refresh() and prints success message; returns 0. No claim about return value is made.
main() default | medium | default check() returns 0 if ok, 1 otherwise; first_run returns 1. Comment says 'Fail CLOSED, matching `daedalus map --check`' – uncheckable.

handoff.purpose: Complete DriftReport assembly with ignore/acceptance logic, and expose refresh() and main() entry points.

symbols.name: refresh
symbols.note: Re-baselines snapshot; carries acceptances forward verbatim.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entry point for drift checking; supports --refresh, --init, and default check.

claims.text: An ABSENT key reads as "nothing was excluded", not as "do not check". Deleting the field must not be a quieter way to narrow the run than setting the variable was.
claims.why: Code: old_ignore = snapshot.get("ignore"); if not isinstance(old_ignore, dict): old_ignore = {"env": "", "file": ""}. Absent key returns None, which is not a dict, so defaults to empty strings. Deleting the field would also cause None, same default. So the claim holds.

claims.text: Only ACCEPTABLE_KINDS count as a match. An acceptance still sitting on an island that has since been wired matches a NOW REACHED item, and must go stale rather than quietly ride along on the good news.
claims.why: Code: if item.kind in ACCEPTABLE_KINDS: by_key.setdefault(item.key, []).append(item). Only items in ACCEPTABLE_KINDS are added to by_key. Later, if an acceptance matches nothing (not in by_key), it becomes STALE_ACCEPTANCE. So the claim is kept.

claims.text: Acceptances are carried forward verbatim -- refreshing is never a way to quietly drop somebody's stated reason.
claims.why: The code calls parse_acceptances(old.get("acceptances")) and then write_snapshot(snap_path, result.state, acceptances). The parse_acceptances function is not defined in this chunk, so we cannot verify that acceptances are carried forward verbatim. The claim is uncheckable.

claims.text: CI gate, not a pre-commit hook: it parses the whole tree and takes seconds.
claims.why: The claim about parsing the whole tree and taking seconds cannot be verified from this code chunk alone.

claims.text: A missing snapshot fails, so deleting it is never a green run
claims.why: The behavior when snapshot is missing is not shown in this chunk; it depends on check() which is defined elsewhere.

observations.what: The ignore drift comparison uses old_ignore from snapshot and new_ignore from state; if they differ, a DriftItem is appended with kind IGNORE_DRIFT.
Acceptance matching logic: only items in ACCEPTABLE_KINDS are considered for matching; invalid, expired, or unmatched acceptances generate appropriate DriftItems.
observations.where: comment before by_key and subsequent for loop

observations.what: main() returns 1 on first_run (missing snapshot) or when report.ok is False; returns 0 on success. The --init flag returns 1 if snapshot exists, else 0.
